minutes.headline: Zoning Board appeared to approve a special permit for a reduced front setback at 54 Maple Parkway, with conditions.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard one application from Kenneth Tully for a special permit to vary the front setback so a new house could replace a trailer on a lot split by wetlands. The conservation and health memos were read, no one from the public spoke, and a motion to approve with conditions was made and seconded. The ayes were heard but the captions do not give a clear count.

votes.motion: Approve the special permit with conditions, including that the Conservation Commission's existing requirements continue.

decisions.decision: The chair explained that a special permit needs all four members present to vote in favor, and offered the applicant the choice of continuing tonight or waiting for a five-member board.
The permit was approved with the condition that the Conservation Commission's existing requirements continue. The captions give only 'aye' calls, not a count.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals appeared to approve a special permit for a reduced front setback at 54 Maple Parkway, with conditions; the vote count is not audible.
The condition attached is that the Conservation Commission's existing requirements continue; the captions record only 'aye' calls, not a count.
The application would let a new house replace a trailer on a lot split by wetlands; the Conservation and Board of Health memos were read.
The chair explained that a special permit needs all four members present to vote in favor, and offered the applicant the choice to continue or wait for a five-member board.
No one from the public spoke on the application.

why_it_matters: A setback permit decides how close a new house may sit to the street, and on a wetland-split lot the Conservation conditions govern what can be built.
